title: Signal and Machine Anew
premise: Paloma Brightwater, a memory-smuggler who has spent fifteen years hauling contraband recollections past orbital customs, is hired to escort a salvage crew to the Meridian, a ship returned from deep space with its crew aged backward and their memories intact but reversed. The reversal was caused by a signal from the relay at the edge of dead space — a signal that will soon reach inhabited systems unless someone reaches the relay first. Racing rival smugglers, corporate hunters, and his own unraveling sense of self as the ship's residual field begins reversing him too, Paloma must choose between destroying the relay (and the Meridian's crew's only chance at restoration) or using it to restore them at the cost of spreading the signal. He finds a third path: overwriting the relay with a counter-signal built from his own smuggled memories, sacrificing his past to buy the future.
about_author: Ada Hartwell is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relay arrays before turning to fiction. Her work explores what survives when memory, identity, and distance are stretched to breaking.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Paloma Brightwater runs a shipment of illegal memories through orbital customs, narrowly evading a scan by hiding the cargo inside his own recall of his mother's death. POV: Paloma. The beat establishes his trade, his loneliness, and the quiet erosion smuggling inflicts on the self he protects so carefully for others.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: Docked at Ceres Station, Paloma witnesses the Meridian's return: a salvage hulk carrying a crew aged backward into youth, lucid but living their lives in reverse order. Corporate agents seal the dock. POV alternates between Paloma and Ilsa Vann, the Meridian's youngest-again captain. The beat is wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Job No One Should Take
chapters.summary: Ilsa hires Paloma: she has traced the reversal to a signal originating at Relay Kestrel in dead space, and needs a smuggler who can outrun the corporate blockade to reach it before the signal propagates further. POV: Paloma. He refuses, then discovers the residual field aboard the Meridian has already begun reversing fragments of his own memory. Fear drives him to accept.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: Paloma threads the Meridian through a corporate interdiction net, burning smuggler tricks fifteen years in the making while corporate hunter Captain Oduya closes in. POV: Paloma, with flashbacks surfacing out of order — the first sign of his deterioration. The beat is kinetic desperation and the first real cost of the mission.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Remembers First
chapters.summary: In transit, Ilsa reveals her reversed life: she remembers her deathbed and not her daughter's birth, and she believes restoration at Kestrel is possible if the signal source is preserved rather than destroyed. Paloma argues for destruction. POV: Ilsa. The beat is intimate grief and the moral fault line that will split the crew.

chapters.title: The Rival
chapters.summary: Smuggler Sef Amari, an old partner Paloma betrayed years ago, intercepts them — hired by the corporation to bring back the Meridian or its evidence. A boarding skirmish ends in stalemate; Sef joins them under uneasy truce when he learns Paloma is reversing too. POV: Sef. The beat is old wounds reopened and grudging alliance.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Crossing dead space, all communications die and the reversal accelerates: Paloma loses whole years, forgetting his mother entirely, while Ilsa grows younger and more disoriented. They find a derelict waystation holding records of an earlier expedition that never came back. POV: Paloma. The beat is existential terror — survival here means losing the self that survives.

chapters.title: Relay Kestrel
chapters.summary: They reach the relay and discover it is not a weapon but an experiment: a research station's attempt to broadcast restored time to a dying colony, gone wrong. Oduya's hunters arrive, demanding the relay be seized for corporate exploitation. POV: rotating among Paloma, Ilsa, and Sef. The beat is revelation colliding with armed standoff.

chapters.title: The Counter-Signal
chapters.summary: Climax. Paloma realizes the relay can be overwritten: a dense enough human memory-web could anchor a counter-signal restoring the Meridian's crew without propagation. It requires a mind full of smuggled memories — his own. As Oduya attacks and Sef holds the docking ring, Paloma uploads everything he is. POV: Paloma. The beat is sacrifice transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: Signal and Machine Anew
chapters.summary: The counter-signal fires; the Meridian's crew begins aging forward again, and the relay goes silent forever. Paloma wakes with no past but a name given him by Ilsa, choosing to build new memories among people who remember for him. POV: Isla closing, watching Paloma begin again. The beat is grief braided with grace — identity rebuilt from witness, not record.
